name: LegionWareX
summary: A medieval high-fantasy adventure sandbox built around Bloom Level-Up: dragons, monsters, bosses, magic, knights, shaders and Fresh Animations, with Better Combat. Minecraft 1.20.1 (Forge).
_comment: FreshOrangeSlices' LegionWareX (2026-10-26), from the Medieval High Fantasy master list and goals docs: a sandbox full of optional content, no required ending, dangerous but not miserable, multiplayer first. Combat route: Better Combat (not Epic Fight); Better Mob Combat is shelved (its mob animation hook crashes the server on creatures from Mowzie's, Migamigos, Cataclysm, Legendary Monsters and Monster Expansion, and with the whole pack on vanilla wolves too; its last build is from January 2025). After the first playtest: Novum's Altitude out (its sky effects made the world disorienting), Ice and Fire out (its dragons wreck buildings, and its 1.20.1 build is a beta), Mowzie's Mobs out, and a bosses layer in their place. Magic: Iron's Spells, plus the RPG Series' Paladins & Priests and Rogues & Warriors (no Wizards, Elemental Wizards or Archers). No voice chat (friends should be able to join with nothing extra). Mods are in cumulative layers so CI can tell which layer breaks what; the shipped pack is every layer. Forge 47.4.28 (1.20.1's recommended; Iron's Spells and others need 47.4+). Modrinth projects by slug (newest 1.20.1 Forge release or beta; required dependencies are added automatically, and the few a mod needs without saying so on Modrinth, such as Iron's Lib, are listed next to it; Migamigos' Framework is CurseForge-only, so it's packed inside). Bloom and the CurseForge-only mods ('external') are packed inside, which is fine for sharing with friends but not for publishing.

layers.name: core
layers._comment: Bloom with Better Combat and the Fresh Animations set (the earlier Forge pack), plus the performance mods, since they change how everything renders: Embeddium, ModernFix, FerriteCore, Clumps, Entity Culling (doesn't draw what's out of sight), ImmediatelyFast (faster HUD and text drawing), AI Improvements (cheaper mob AI), Let Me Despawn (mobs that picked up items still despawn, dropping them), and for the server, Chunky (pre-generate the world) and spark (find what lags).

layers.name: creatures
layers._comment: Creatures, bosses and companions, and the spawn and structure control that keeps them memorable instead of everywhere.

layers.name: magic-and-gear
layers._comment: Iron's Spells as the mage, the RPG Series' Paladins & Priests and Rogues & Warriors (Spell Engine comes with them), weapons and armor, and the recipe glue for all of it. Marium's Soulslike Weaponry is on test (power creep).

layers.name: animation-and-qol
layers._comment: The rest of the visual stack (Punchy! stays unless testing shows it fights Better Combat; Oculus, the Forge port of Iris, with Complementary Unbound picked, Solas to swap to, and MakeUp Ultra Fast for weaker PCs), and the quality-of-life and multiplayer mods.

layers.name: bosses
layers._comment: Bosses in place of Ice and Fire and Mowzie's Mobs (first playtest): L_Ender's Cataclysm (dungeon bosses), Legendary Monsters (roaming early, middle and late game bosses), Bosses'Rise (Souls-like bosses), The Graveyard (graveyards, crypts and their undead) and Illager Invasion (new illagers to fight), Bosses Oddities (more unusual bosses; CurseForge-only, packed inside) and GTBC's Cataclysmic Boss UI (a screen before each Cataclysm boss fight with its lore, attacks and tips), the last two FreshOrangeSlices' picks. CI summons every one of their creatures with the rest of the pack.

config_files._comment: For both sides (the server, and the worlds a player makes; Forge copies defaultconfigs into each new world). A safety net: an entity or block entity that errors while ticking is removed and logged instead of crashing the server. Legionary's Unbreakable boss shoots flaming skulls and magma blocks whose code needs a client-only class, so each one crashes a dedicated server on its first tick (found by the mob check); with this they fizzle instead.

client_presets._resource_packs: Bottom to top, above vanilla's Default (and Forge's mod resources). Bloom switches them on before the game first reads options.txt, once per change of this list (client/mixin/OptionsMixin).
client_presets._shader: Shaders on with Complementary Unbound at first launch (and once per change of this line); K turns shaders off, O picks another pack (Solas and the much lighter MakeUp Ultra Fast ship too).
client_presets._keys: Key bindings set once per change of this list (by name, as options.txt has them): Oculus's 'reload shaders' is unbound (it was R, and a stray press freezes the game for seconds while the shader rebuilds).

files._comment: Client config files, as given (the mod fills in every setting left out). FreshOrangeSlices wants Minecraft's own title screen: Aquamirae swaps in its frozen-sea panorama and logo.
